images.caption: Figure 2:Motivation of multi-concept scene sketch generation.(A) Widely used in animation, concept art, and design. (B) Artists adjust sketch refinement from draft to detailed sketch preserving structure for different goals.

Figure 3:SketchDirectorpipeline. Given a scene description,SketchDirectorfirst generates object-level draft assets. The agent then progressively composes the scene through executable operations from the action library, maintaining scene programs and spatial asset attributes. A closed-loop process iteratively adjusts the layout, supported by self-evolving memory that incorporates short-term failure feedback and long-term experiences. Finally, detail refinement employs curve contour resampling and progressive joint optimization to enhance sketch details while preserving the established scene layout and object structures.

Figure 4:Example agentic reasoning trajectory inSketchDirector.A real log illustrating how agents interleave layout planning, scene state updates, geometric-semantic verification, memory evolution, and correction.

Figure 5:A success example of planning and execution inSketchDirector.Each operation updates both the executable program and the represented scene state, yielding a traceable trajectory from the initial drafts to the final layout.

Figure 6:Qualitative comparison with existing methods.Compared withLLM-based methods, our sketch generation produces scene sketches with more explicit object organization, coherent layouts, and better visual-semantic alignment.
Moreover, compared withoptimization-based methods, our refinement improves sketch details while faithfully preserving the object layouts and spatial relationships in the draft.

Figure 7:Scene sketch diversity generated by SketchDirector.Our object-level reasoning enables flexible scene layouts from textual descriptions, by producing diverse spatial arrangements (the top row) and object configurations under similar semantic descriptions (the bottom row).
Figure 9:Qualitative comparison of different VLM backbones.Visual results highlight differences in object-level sketch fidelity, scene composition, and visual details across backbone models.
Figure 10:Qualitative ablation of agentic layout reasoning.Visual results illustrate how individual components affect scene composition and object-level spatial coherence.

Figure 11:Comparison of point-based and curve-based contour resampling method.Curve-based contour resampling preserves object shapes and structural details, providing a more stable initialization for subsequent refinement.

Figure 12:Qualitative ablation of progressive joint optimization.Removing local supervision, global supervision, or progressive optimization leads to degraded object fidelity and scene-level coherence.

modeling complex physical and semantic interactions. (B) Object hallucination during refinement.
